items.title: [macOS Desktop] Repeated finances plugin-cache creation/deletion accompanies MCP refresh bursts and severe lag

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: mcp
labels.description: Issues related to the use of model context protocol (MCP) servers

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: skills
labels.description: Issues related to skills

labels.name: app-server
labels.description: Issues involving app server protocol or interfaces

items.body:
## Environment

- Codex Desktop: 26.930.51102, build 13100
- Bundled CLI: 0.160.0
- Platform: macOS
- Observed October 5, 2026, after updating and restarting the desktop app

## Problem

Codex becomes severely laggy during startup and reply/tool activity, while the computer's fan ramps up. Restarting sometimes produces a quiet interval, but the activity returns.

Read-only filesystem captures show the `finances` plugin cache repeatedly being created and removed. The desktop app-server is directly identified as the deleting process. Separate Codex processes create the cache, but the original caller of the creating operations remains unresolved.

## Captured evidence

### Cache creation/deletion

A two-minute capture started before launching Codex recorded:

- **55 successful cache-root `mkdir` operations.** Their process identities could not be resolved before the syscall threads exited.
- **40 successful cache-root `unlinkat` operations**, directly attributed to the local desktop app-server.

An earlier capture attributed one successful creation to a separate short-lived Codex process. Approximately **236 milliseconds after that creation**, the desktop app-server successfully removed the cache-root entry. The creating process exited before its original caller or subcommand could be established.

These counts are filesystem operations, not necessarily 55 distinct bundle downloads or complete reinstalls.

### Repeated plugin and MCP refresh activity

A diagnostic session repeatedly logged `completed remote installed plugin bundle sync`, with `finances@openai-curated-remote` in `changed_plugins`, empty materializations, and no failed plugin IDs.

Separately sampled windows showed:

- **1,278 MCP ready notifications in 60 seconds**, with no starting or failed statuses.
- **6,898 MCP startup/status notifications in approximately four minutes** after a restart. That window also included Cloudflare reauthentication failures and n8n HTTP 429 failures; those failures are distinct from the repeated healthy-ready notifications.

The local `finances` manifest declares Apps capability and no MCP servers. There is no `finances` entry in the root TOML plugins table, although that alone does not establish its remote installation state.

## Steps to reproduce in the affected installation

1. Quit Codex normally.
2. Start a read-only filesystem trace and process-identity tracker before launching the app.
3. Launch Codex with the existing chats and MCP configuration.
4. Use the ordinary chat interface and observe startup/reply lag and fan activity.
5. Inspect filtered cache operations and bounded desktop logs for repeated plugin changes and MCP status/inventory activity.

This is reproducible in an existing installation. A minimal clean-install reproduction has not been isolated.

## Expected behavior

The plugin cache should stabilize after startup. Unchanged plugin state and healthy MCP readiness should not repeatedly trigger global inventory/runtime refresh work. Actual installation, authentication, and tool changes should still propagate.

## Investigation request and limitations

Please investigate which component recreates the `finances` cache and why the desktop app-server repeatedly removes it. One possibility is disagreement between installed-plugin views used by components sharing the cache, but this is a hypothesis.

The cache churn, repeated refresh activity, and lag are observed together; a controlled test has not yet established the complete causal chain or how much each contributes to latency. A brief pause/resume test of the remote execution helper was inconclusive and did not provide a lasting fix.

Related: https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/50627 describes sustained unchanged-ready notifications and inventory refresh traffic. This report adds directly captured cache creation/deletion evidence.

Only sanitized aggregate diagnostics are included. No credentials, account identifiers, hostnames, device identifiers, private paths, raw logs, or chat content are included.

items.title: [macOS Computer Use] Cmd+A sends Cmd+Q on Belgian AZERTY and quits target apps

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

Installed ChatGPT/Codex desktop bundle: **26.930.51102 (build 13100)**, read from the installed app's Info.plist. The About dialog was not inspected.

Computer-use JavaScript package: **`@oai/sky` 0.7.5**. Tool surface: **`mcp__cua_repl.js`**, using native macOS app input.

### What subscription do you have?

Not included.

### What platform is your computer?

**macOS 26.6.2 (build 25G83), Apple Silicon (arm64)**.

`uname -mprs`: `Darwin 25.6.0 arm64 arm`.

Active user keyboard input source reported by macOS preferences: **`com.apple.keylayout.Belgian`** (Belgian AZERTY).

### What issue are you seeing?

Native Computer Use sends **Command+Q (Quit)** when an agent requests **Command+A (Select All)** using the documented `pressKey("super+a")` API.

This caused Safari to disappear during a form-editing task and UltiMaker Cura to disappear twice while the agent was trying to replace a print-setting value. In both Cura incidents, the action sequence included clicking the field and then requesting `super+a`. The Safari trace shows the same shortcut immediately before the original window was replaced by a Start Page.

The agent was attempting to select text, not requesting Quit. This interrupts ongoing tasks and risks losing unsaved work. Reading the app state afterward can relaunch the app and make the failure look like a window/capture problem; Cura subsequently appeared with an empty plate.

The keyboard mismatch was independently reproduced in a disposable AppKit probe window, without touching the user documents or browser tabs. Its Quit menu handler only recorded the command instead of terminating, so the test was safe.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. On macOS, make Belgian AZERTY the active keyboard input source.
2. Open a disposable native AppKit test app with an editable text field, a Select All menu item whose key equivalent is `a`, and a Quit menu item whose key equivalent is `q`. Instrument key-down events and menu actions; make the probe's Quit handler log instead of terminating.
3. Bind that app through Computer Use. Initialization is a separate tool call:

```js
let probe = await cua.getApp("/path/to/KeyboardProbe.app");
```

4. In the next tool call, send the documented Select All shortcut:

```js
await probe.pressKey("super+a");
await probe.getAXState();
```

5. Inspect the probe log. The actual recorded output from the reproduction on 2026-10-05 was:

```text
READY
KEY: keyCode=0 characters=q command=true
COMMAND: Quit (Cmd+Q)
```

The probe recorded each `NSEvent.keyDown` with:

```swift
monitor = NSEvent.addLocalMonitorForEvents(matching: .keyDown) { event in
    record("KEY: keyCode=\(event.keyCode) characters=\(event.charactersIgnoringModifiers ?? "") command=\(event.modifierFlags.contains(.command))")
    return event
}
```

Its menu commands used the normal AppKit key equivalents `q` and `a`. The Quit handler recorded `COMMAND: Quit (Cmd+Q)`.

### What is the expected behavior?

`pressKey("super+a")` should invoke **Select All** under the active Belgian AZERTY keyboard layout. It must not invoke Quit.

Named letter shortcuts should resolve consistently with the active macOS input source. If the API intentionally uses physical key positions, that distinction needs to be explicit and a layout-aware way to request logical shortcuts should be available.

### Additional information

- The deterministic probe confirms the emitted **keyCode 0 / character q / Command** event and the resulting Quit command. This is separate from the agent's interpretation of the UI afterward.
- The native input appears to use the QWERTY physical position for `a` without resolving the active AZERTY layout. This is an inference from the received event; the native implementation was not inspected or patched.
- In the Cura task, the post-action errors included `Computer Use server error -10005: noWindowsAvailable` and, on the second attempt, `Computer Use is not active ... You first must call get_app_state ...`. These are follow-on observations, not evidence of the original cause.
- A control using `probe.setValue(1, "Safe replacement verified")` successfully updated the field and left the probe window open.
- The diagnostic chat used **gpt-6.1-sol**. Reproduction uses an explicit tool call; behavior across other models was not tested.
- Temporary workaround: avoid native `super+a`, use accessibility value replacement/text selection or the app's Select All menu, and inspect the state after each input action. Local skill and agent instructions have been updated accordingly; the runtime bug remains.
- Suggested regression coverage: `super+a` on Belgian AZERTY, French AZERTY, and U.S. QWERTY, asserting Select All rather than Quit in a disposable native test app.
- Only the synthetic probe output is included here; private task content and full session transcripts are omitted.

items.title: Force fresh Guardian sessions for parent-checkpoint recovery
items.body:
Force fresh Guardian sessions for parent-checkpoint recovery

## Why

A Guardian review restarting from the parent checkpoint must bypass cached reviewer sessions and snapshots, even when another review is using the cached session.

## What changed

- Add `ReviewerRequest::requires_fresh_session` and enable it for parent-checkpoint recovery.
- Replace an idle cached session with a fresh reusable session, or start a fresh ephemeral session when the cached session is busy. Neither recovery path inherits a cached snapshot.
- Reserve the review permit before validating a cached session and before exposing a newly spawned session to concurrent requests.

## Testing

Add tests covering recovery with idle and busy cached sessions, verifying that recovery receives no cached snapshot and that subsequent reviews reuse the appropriate session.

items.title: [Feature Request] Public Codex Desktop Extension API / Extension Host

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: skills
labels.description: Issues related to skills

items.body:
## Summary

Codex Desktop is increasingly becoming a primary development workspace rather than just a chat client. However, most of its native UI and workspace functionality is currently fixed and cannot be extended by users.

I would like Codex Desktop to expose a public extension API, similar in spirit to the VS Code Extension API, so that developers can build native integrations around Codex workflows without modifying or forking the app itself.

Existing Codex plugins, skills, MCP servers, and hooks are useful for extending agent capabilities, but they do not provide sufficient control over the **desktop UI and workspace layer**.

The missing piece is a set of stable **UI contribution points and workspace APIs**.

## Motivation

There are already several related feature requests around:

- VS Code-like plugin systems
- file explorer / repository trees
- custom buttons and commands
- configurable workspace layouts
- richer plugin UI
- remote workspace file management

Instead of implementing these individually, a public extension API could provide the foundation for users and third-party developers to build them.

### 1. Better File Explorer

A developer could implement a VS Code-like file explorer with:

- persistent directory tree
- file creation / rename / delete / move
- Git status decorations
- drag and drop
- context menus
- remote filesystem support
- custom file viewers

This would allow users to improve the file manager without requiring the Codex team to implement every workflow directly.

### 2. Training / GPU Task Monitor

For ML and robotics workflows, it would be useful to add a native sidebar panel showing:

- local and remote machines
- running jobs
- GPU utilization
- process status
- recent logs
- training progress
- failed/stalled jobs

For example:

```text
Codex
├── Chats
├── Files
├── Git
└── Training Monitor
    ├── gpu-server-01
    │   ├── job: humanoid_policy_train
    │   ├── GPU 0: 94%
    │   └── status: running
    └── gpu-server-02
        └── idle
```

The backend can already be implemented through MCP, SSH, scripts, or other integrations. What is currently missing is a supported way to expose this information as a persistent Codex Desktop UI.

### 3. Robotics / ROS Dashboard

For robotics development, extensions could expose:

- ROS nodes/topics
- robot status
- simulation state
- camera streams
- policy rollout state
- experiment controls

Codex could then act as both an agent interface and a development control plane.

### 4. Git / Jupyter / Data Viewers

Extensions could also provide:

- Git Graph
- Jupyter notebook viewer
- TensorBoard integration
- dataset browser
- PDF/video viewers
- experiment dashboards

## Proposed API Surface

An MVP does not need to expose the entire Codex UI.

A small set of stable contribution points would already enable many workflows.

### Commands

```ts
codex.commands.registerCommand(
  "training.restart",
  () => restartTraining()
);
```

### Sidebar Views

```ts
codex.window.registerSidebarView(
  "training-monitor",
  provider
);
```

### Panels / Webviews

```ts
const panel = codex.window.createWebviewPanel(
  "gpu-monitor",
  "GPU Monitor"
);
```

A sandboxed WebView API similar to VS Code would probably be sufficient for many third-party integrations.

### Workspace API

```ts
codex.workspace.fs.readFile(...)
codex.workspace.fs.writeFile(...)
codex.workspace.onDidChangeFiles(...)
```

### Current Context

```ts
codex.context.currentWorkspace
codex.context.currentThread
codex.context.selectedFile
```

This is particularly important because extensions often need to associate external tools with the user's current Codex task.

### Task / Thread State

An API for observing Codex execution state would also be extremely useful:

```ts
codex.tasks.getRunningTasks()
codex.tasks.onDidChangeTaskState(...)
codex.threads.getCurrentThread()
```

This could enable task dashboards and monitoring extensions without requiring fragile UI automation.

### File Viewer / Editor Contributions

```ts
codex.workspace.registerFileViewer(...)
codex.workspace.registerEditor(...)
```

This would allow third parties to add viewers for notebooks, robotics logs, videos, simulation artifacts, etc.

## Architecture

Conceptually:

```text
                       Codex Desktop
                             │
               ┌─────────────┴─────────────┐
               │                           │
       Codex / Agent Runtime          Extension Host
               │                           │
       Skills / MCP / Hooks       commands / views / panels
               │                  workspace / tasks / editors
               │                           │
               └─────────────┬─────────────┘
                             │
                        User Extensions
```

The existing plugin system could remain responsible for agent-side capabilities, while the Extension Host provides desktop-side integration.

An extension could combine both:

```text
Extension
├── MCP server
├── skills
├── hooks
└── desktop UI
    ├── sidebar
    ├── commands
    └── panels
```

## Security

Extensions obviously introduce a larger security surface.

A permission model could therefore be explicit, for example:

```json
{
  "permissions": [
    "workspace.read",
    "workspace.write",
    "tasks.read",
    "network",
    "webview"
  ]
}
```

Codex could show these permissions before installing an extension.

Extensions could also run in a sandboxed extension host rather than inside the main application process.

## Why this matters

Codex is already moving beyond a traditional coding assistant toward an agentic development environment.

As more workflows move into Codex—coding, remote execution, research, ML experiments, robotics, long-running tasks—the number of domain-specific UI requirements will grow rapidly.

It is unlikely that the Codex team can or should implement every specialized UI directly.

A stable extension API would allow the ecosystem to solve the long tail of these workflows.

Instead of asking:

> Should Codex add a better file explorer?

the more scalable question may be:

> Can Codex provide the primitives needed for users to build one?

## Related Issues

This proposal overlaps with several existing requests, including:

- #36649 — VS Code-like plugin system
- #23237 — Rich interactive plugin / custom UI
- #37824 — Custom UI buttons / commands
- #46588 — First-class file workspace
- #34701 — File explorer tree

It may make sense to treat a Desktop Extension API as an umbrella architecture that enables many of these features rather than solving each one independently.

## Suggested MVP

A minimal first version could expose only:

1. `registerCommand()`
2. `registerSidebarView()`
3. `createWebviewPanel()`
4. workspace filesystem access
5. current workspace/thread context
6. task-state events

Even this small API would enable a substantial ecosystem of Codex-native developer tools.

items.title: Recover Guardian reviews from parent checkpoints
items.body:
Recover Guardian reviews from parent checkpoints

## Why

Reviewer compaction can invalidate previously admitted transcript evidence. When a parent checkpoint is available, restarting from that checkpoint preserves the captured parent context instead of relying on a lossy reviewer summary.

## What changed

- Restart an invalidated reviewer once from the action-time parent checkpoint, within the original review deadline.
- Preserve fresh checkpoints during startup and fit review input using the existing budget selection.
- Select transcript evidence from the checkpoint actually loaded by the reviewer. Track the transcript source so cursors remain valid across legacy-history eviction and reset when the source changes.
- Resume transcript deltas after successful recovery, including authorization added after the parent checkpoint.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for checkpoint recovery, post-checkpoint authorization, resumed deltas, and stopping after one restart. Extend history tests to cover both legacy retention and parent-checkpoint reuse, and update the checkpoint-migration snapshot.

items.title: [Desktop SSH] Linux-to-Mac sync replaces active host bundled plugins with a Visualize-only catalog

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: skills
labels.description: Issues related to skills

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

- Target Mac desktop: `26.930.31730`, build `12947`.
- Controller Linux desktop: official `chatgpt` package `26.930.41038`.
- I also downloaded and inspected official Linux candidate `26.930.51102`. Its relevant sync implementation still has this collision. This candidate was **not installed or tested as a running app**.

### What subscription do you have?

Not disclosed.

### What platform is your computer?

- Target: `Darwin 27.0.0 arm64 arm`.
- Controller: `Linux 7.0.0-38-generic x86_64 unknown`.

### What issue are you seeing?

Enabling Linux desktop SSH access to a Mac that is already running the desktop app replaces the Mac's full generated `openai-bundled` marketplace with a **Visualize-only** marketplace. Computer Use, Chrome, and Browser then disappear from plugin discovery even though the Mac app bundle still contains them.

The affected folder is:

```text
<Mac CODEX_HOME>/.tmp/bundled-marketplaces/openai-bundled
```

Native requests fail with errors such as:

```text
plugin `computer-use` was not found in marketplace `openai-bundled`
plugin `chrome` was not found in marketplace `openai-bundled`
plugin `browser` was not found in marketplace `openai-bundled`
```

This is a repeatable conflict between two desktop clients writing one catalog, rather than missing files in the installation. The Mac's OpenAI signature and sealed resources verify. `dpkg -V chatgpt` on Linux reports no modified package files.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Run the desktop app on the Mac with Computer Use, Chrome, and Browser installed/enabled.
2. Configure and enable the Linux desktop app's SSH connection to the same Mac user and `CODEX_HOME`.
3. Inspect the target's generated marketplace before and after the outgoing controller-side bundled-plugin sync.
4. The target manifest now lists only `visualize`, and its other bundled plugin directories have been removed.
5. Request Computer Use/Chrome/Browser from the Mac desktop. Plugin discovery reports them missing.

The observed controller log recorded:

- SSH connected: `2026-10-04T23:57:44.820Z`.
- Visualize-only remote marketplace sync: `2026-10-04T23:57:45.395Z`.

The target manifest and `.materialization-key` changed at that same second. The target's stored SHA256 marker exactly matches the controller's Visualize payload when hashed with the Mac destination paths.

### What is the expected behavior?

Connecting through SSH must preserve plugins owned by the target's active desktop app. I need Linux-to-Mac SSH access and the Mac's existing Computer Use/browser features to coexist.

### Additional information

**Owning implementation identified in the shipped desktop JavaScript:**

- The local desktop materializer and outgoing SSH materializer both choose `<CODEX_HOME>/.tmp/bundled-marketplaces/openai-bundled` on the target.
- Only Visualize is marked `syncToRemoteSshHosts: true` in the inspected builds.
- The SSH writer computes a payload SHA256 and checks `.materialization-key`. If it differs, it recursively removes the entire destination marketplace root, then writes the reduced catalog and plugin files.
- The local desktop writer uses the same marker filename for JSON metadata containing app version, bundle identity, and plugin information.
- After copying, SSH reconciliation explicitly registers the generated folder as the marketplace source again.

**Additional reproduction without damaging active state:**

I extracted the remote write function from official candidate `26.930.51102` and exercised it with an in-memory filesystem/transport adapter and synthetic plugin files. This is an isolated function test, not a full candidate-app runtime test.

| Initial state / trigger | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Full catalog with local desktop JSON marker | Whole root replaced; only Visualize remains |
| Full catalog restored while retaining matching remote SHA256 marker; identical reconnect | Full restored catalog survives; no replacement |
| Local JSON marker regenerated | Whole root replaced again; only Visualize remains |
| Remote plugin payload changes | Whole root replaced again; only Visualize remains |

**Recovery and limits:**

Restoring the generated files from the signed Mac app bundle while preserving the matching remote SHA256 marker recovered this session. After re-enabling SSH, native Chrome clicking/typing, Chrome extension page reading/navigation, in-app browser navigation, and a read-only app-server RPC through Linux SSH to the Mac all passed. User configuration was unchanged. This recovery is temporary: marker regeneration or payload changes can retrigger the overwrite.

I also tried registering the intact signed app bundle as an alternative marketplace source in an isolated `CODEX_HOME`. The supported command rejected it with `marketplace openai-bundled is reserved and cannot be added from this source` (backticks omitted here). No active configuration was changed.

Please separate SSH and desktop catalog ownership, or merge/preserve the target's desktop entries safely. A fix should cover reconnect after local regeneration, both startup orderings, and controller/target updates. A supported way to disable only outgoing bundled-marketplace sync would also help, provided SSH and target-side features remain available.

Related reports: #25780 and #25809 concern bundled catalog loss; #34263 concerns a different SSH browser-provisioning direction. This report identifies the outgoing SSH writer replacing an **already active target desktop's** catalog with a reduced subset.

No app bundle patch, broad cache deletion, wrapper, watcher, immutable flags, state migration, or reinstall was applied. Private paths, host aliases, credentials, and raw logs are omitted.

items.title: Feature Request: Isolated Windows GUI testing using RDP Child Sessions

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
### What variant of Codex are you using?

App

### What feature would you like to see?

# Summary

Please consider adding an **isolated/background GUI testing mode on Windows** using Windows **RDP Child Sessions**.

Computer Use is extremely useful for developing desktop applications, but having an AI coding agent interact with the user's actual desktop is disruptive: mouse/keyboard interaction, focus changes, window management, screenshots, overlays, and application launches interfere with the developer who is using the same machine.

Windows already provides an OS-level mechanism that appears particularly well suited for this use case: **RDP Child Sessions**.

This would allow the coding agent to operate a complete interactive Windows desktop in a separate local session while the developer continues working normally in the parent session.

# Current problem

A common coding-agent workflow is:

    edit code
        ↓
    build
        ↓
    launch application
        ↓
    inspect UI
        ↓
    click / type / interact
        ↓
    verify behavior
        ↓
    modify code
        ↓
    repeat

For desktop application development, this loop becomes disruptive when Computer Use operates on the developer's interactive desktop.

Ideally:

    Developer session                 Agent session

    IDE                               Application under test
    Browser                           Screenshots / vision
    Terminal                          Mouse / keyboard automation
    Normal desktop usage              UI Automation
                                      GUI testing

              both running simultaneously

The developer's mouse, keyboard, foreground window and desktop should remain unaffected while the agent tests the application.

# Windows already has an interesting mechanism for this

Windows supports **RDP Child Sessions**, introduced with Windows 8 / Windows Server 2012.

This is not conventional Remote Desktop to another machine or VM.

A Child Session is a special **local loopback Remote Desktop session associated with the existing user's session**.

Microsoft exposes APIs including:

- `WTSEnableChildSessions`
- `WTSIsChildSessionsEnabled`
- `WTSGetChildSessionId`
- Remote Desktop ActiveX Control
- `IMsRdpExtendedSettings::Property("ConnectToChildSession")`

With `ConnectToChildSession = TRUE`, an embedded RDP client can connect to the local Child Session.

Conceptually:

    Codex
            │
            ▼
    Parent Windows Session
            │
            ├── Developer keeps working normally
            │
            └── RDP Child Session
                    │
                    ├── Application under test
                    ├── screenshot / vision
                    ├── mouse + keyboard interaction
                    ├── UI Automation
                    └── automated GUI testing

This is conceptually similar to the old Visual Studio / Windows 8 Store App Simulator, which provided a complete interactive Windows environment inside a window without requiring a full VM.

# Why Child Sessions instead of only background HWND automation?

Window-scoped capture and background input are useful and should absolutely remain options.

However, they do not provide a complete isolated desktop environment.

Many applications require real desktop behavior:

- modal dialogs
- multiple application windows
- popup menus
- drag & drop
- focus handling
- native file dialogs
- clipboard interaction
- applications using custom rendering
- GPU-rendered UI
- applications without useful accessibility/UIA trees
- workflows involving multiple processes

A separate Windows Child Session could support these scenarios while still leaving the developer's parent session alone.

This could therefore complement window-scoped/background automation rather than replace it.

Possible modes could be:

    1. Window-scoped background automation
       → lightweight, single HWND

    2. RDP Child Session
       → complete isolated interactive desktop

    3. Current desktop Computer Use
       → full interaction with the user's session

# Example workflow

1. The coding agent modifies a WPF/WinForms/WinUI/MAUI/Win32 application.
2. It builds the application.
3. It launches the application inside its Windows Child Session.
4. Computer Use captures the Child Session instead of the user's desktop.
5. The agent interacts with the application.
6. It discovers a visual or behavioral problem.
7. It modifies the source code and rebuilds.
8. It restarts the application inside the Child Session.
9. It verifies the fix.

Meanwhile, the developer can continue using the parent Windows session normally.

This could enable a genuinely autonomous:

    edit → build → run → inspect → interact → fix → repeat

loop without the AI agent effectively taking over the developer's computer.

## Existing related requests / evidence

For Codex, this is closely related to:

**openai/codex #41323**
"[Windows][Computer Use] Add target-window-only capture, background input, and no-overlay mode for desktop EXE automation"

That issue addresses essentially the same developer pain point through HWND-scoped capture and background input.

RDP Child Sessions could provide an additional OS-native solution for cases where window-scoped automation is insufficient.

There are also third-party projects experimenting with Windows Child Sessions for AI/desktop automation, demonstrating that the concept is practical rather than purely theoretical.

Microsoft still documents the Child Session APIs:

- Child Sessions — Remote Desktop Services
- `WTSEnableChildSessions`
- `WTSIsChildSessionsEnabled`
- `WTSGetChildSessionId`
- `IMsRdpExtendedSettings`
- `ConnectToChildSession`

The feature has existed since Windows 8 / Windows Server 2012.

# Why I think this is particularly useful for coding agents

General-purpose Computer Use sometimes needs to control the user's actual desktop.

Coding agents are different.

During application development, the GUI being controlled is often an **application created specifically by the current coding task**.

There is usually no reason why that application must run on the developer's physical/interactive desktop.

Giving the agent its own interactive Windows session could make GUI development dramatically less intrusive while retaining real Windows desktop semantics.

I would love to see an officially supported "isolated GUI testing" mode based on this or a similar Windows-native mechanism.

items.body:
## Summary

A freshly published Codex Cloud environment executes a setup sequence that is materially different from the Install script currently shown in the published environment configuration, then the task ends with:

`Failed to set up container`

This was reproduced after deleting/replacing the previous published environment and creating a brand-new personal environment from scratch.

Repository: `fn-digital/iso-management-app`  
Visibility: private  
Environment privacy: `Only me`

## Published Install script

The currently published environment visibly contains an Install script that starts with:

```bash
echo "=== ISO Cloud clean environment setup ==="
```

and only performs:

- `corepack enable`
- `corepack prepare pnpm@11.7.0 --activate`
- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`
- PostgreSQL 17 package installation if PostgreSQL 17 is not already installed
- `playwright install --with-deps chromium`
- final version checks

It ends with:

```bash
echo "=== ISO Cloud clean environment dependencies ready ==="
```

It does **not** create a PostgreSQL role/database, run Prisma migrations or seed, or build the API/Web applications.

## What fresh Cloud tasks actually execute

A fresh task instead shows, under `Running setup scripts...`:

```text
=== ISO Management Applicatie — Codex Cloud setup ===
```

and then executes an additional/different setup sequence including:

- `corepack prepare pnpm@11.7.0 --activate`
- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`
- PostgreSQL 17 package installation
- starting the local PostgreSQL 17 cluster
- creating a local PostgreSQL role/database (`iso_management_codex`)
- `pnpm db:generate`
- `pnpm db:migrate`
- `pnpm db:seed`
- API build
- Web build
- Playwright Chromium installation

The setup ends with:

```text
=== Codex Cloud setup complete ===
```

All 40 Prisma migrations apply successfully. Prisma generation, seed, API build, Web build, and Chromium installation also complete successfully.

Despite this, the Cloud task still reports:

`Failed to set up container`

and does not proceed normally to the requested task.

## Reproduction history

1. Earlier environments had legacy/migration/onboarding history and conflicting revisions.
2. To remove those variables, the published environment was replaced with a new personal environment.
3. The new environment was connected to `fn-digital/iso-management-app`.
4. A new Install script and Start skill were entered from scratch.
5. Cloud Environment Onboarding: Setup inspected the repository.
6. Initial onboarding was blocked by network policy (HTTP 403).
7. Onboarding saved the required allowlist. The environment now has 11 explicit allowed domains for npm/Prisma/PostgreSQL/Playwright-related downloads.
8. The environment was successfully saved and published.
9. A completely fresh Cloud task was started.
10. That task still executed the different setup sequence described above and ended with `Failed to set up container`.

The repository remained unchanged during environment troubleshooting.

## Expected behavior

A fresh task should use the currently published environment configuration.

If Codex Cloud intentionally generates or persists another setup layer in addition to the visible Install script, the UI/logs should expose:

- which setup source is being executed;
- the environment configuration ID;
- the published revision ID/hash;
- whether the task was started from the expected published revision.

If the setup itself completes successfully, the task should proceed to agent execution rather than fail generically with `Failed to set up container`.

## Actual behavior

The published environment UI and the task's executed setup sequence diverge, with no visible explanation of where the additional setup comes from.

Because the unexpected setup itself successfully completes the application dependency/database/build steps, this does not currently look like an application-level Prisma/PostgreSQL/build failure.

## Related reports

Similar Cloud startup/provisioning symptoms:

- #47269 — Codex Cloud: “Failed to set up container” on all tasks
- #44265 — Codex Cloud fails at “Downloading repo” before agent execution
- #32209 — Cloud tasks stall at “Running setup scripts” before custom setup script begins
- #51110 — Published environment cannot be reliably selected or runtime-verified across new task launch paths

These may share symptoms without necessarily sharing the same root cause.

## Request

Could the Codex Cloud team inspect whether fresh tasks can be bound to a stale/prepared setup or a different published environment revision than the one shown in the environment editor?

It would also help if the failure UI exposed the underlying provisioning/finalization error instead of only `Failed to set up container`.

I can provide screenshots of:

- the environment showing `Published`;
- the current visible Install script;
- the task setup log showing the different setup sequence.

items.body:
### What variant of Codex are you using?

Codex Desktop, with a shared organization model across ChatGPT Chat, Work, and Codex on desktop, web, and mobile. This is a product-design proposal.

### What feature would you like to see?

**Provide one resource-management entry that connects keywords, conversations, and related resources, with editable tags, project relationships, and resource locations as complementary views.**

#### Current workflow and remaining gap

I use sidebar sections such as Projects, Study, Life, Engineering, and Work to organize tasks and projects. I pin urgent or currently important items and unpin them when that priority passes. When starting a project, I also organize its local repository folders deliberately.

Sections have helped with broad categorization, but they do not fully express project/subproject relationships or connect the discussions and resources belonging to the same work. A conversation may later produce documents, images, code, or a repository. I need to find those outputs together with the discussions that produced them, regardless of which product surface I used.

#### Connect the work through tags

The core relationship should be **keywords ↔ conversations ↔ related resources**.

- Support an extensible keyword/tag vocabulary, with one or several tags usable to retrieve related ChatGPT conversations, Codex tasks, projects, documents, images, repositories, and external links.
- Preserve links between a resource and its originating conversation or task. Where applicable, retain the repository location and relevant Git branch or commit reference.
- Allow the same item to be discoverable through several topics without duplicating the conversation or file.
- Make tags editable, searchable, and mergeable so that similar automatically suggested keywords do not become an unmanageable vocabulary.

#### A possible management interface

One top-level entry could offer three tabs:

- **Tags:** topics that connect work across conversations, projects, and resource types.
- **Projects:** what the work belongs to, including parent/child project relationships.
- **Spaces / resource locations:** where the linked files and repositories actually live.

These names and tabs are a suggested design; the essential requirement is to make the relationships understandable and navigable.

I would keep the main folder/group structure small enough to scan at a glance while allowing the tag vocabulary to grow. The sidebar could show selected important tags or groups. Opening one would reveal its related conversations, projects, and resources in a detail panel. This would give the sidebar a clear role as an entry into the work without requiring it to display a full filesystem tree.

Priority, broad categorization, project hierarchy, and storage location should remain independently manageable. Reorganizing a project in the interface should not require moving its repository on disk.

#### AI-assisted organization

As soon as a new conversation has enough context, AI could suggest one to three initial keywords, even if no code or media has been produced. Suggestions could evolve with the work and remain easy for the user to rename, merge, or remove.

AI could also classify and link resources, propose project relationships, and present the result as an editable visual tree. My work develops dynamically; when returning to it, I need a clear structure that I can inspect and correct.

Classification should initially organize metadata and links. Moving actual files or repositories should be a separate explicit action. Shared tags should not automatically expand access or load every linked resource into every task.

#### Expected outcome

A user could begin discussing an idea, generate a document, and later create a repository. Selecting the relevant topic would bring together the discussion, project, document, repository location, and relevant version references without requiring the user to remember which product surface each item came from.

### Additional information

Related requests:

- #33304 concerns nested local projects. This proposal adds cross-cutting relationships between conversations and resources, alongside project hierarchy.
- #45818 concerns a shared project container across Chat, Work, and Codex. This proposal focuses on how the associated material is organized and retrieved.
- #46836 is my proposal for progressively enabling capabilities within one task. This request addresses resource organization as that task and its outputs evolve.

The examples above describe my workflow and a proposed design. No private project names, paths, conversation contents, or attachments are included.

items.title: Add promise settlement streaming helpers to code mode
items.body:
Add promise settlement streaming helpers to code mode

## What changed

Expose two JavaScript globals for consuming results as inputs settle:

- `as_settled(promises)` returns an async iterator of fulfilled and rejected records in settlement order, preserving queued results while the consumer is busy.
- `stream_settled(promises, emit)` delivers those records to a callback, awaiting each invocation and propagating callback errors.

Records include an `index`, a `status`, and either a `value` or a `reason`. Iterable inputs use positional indices; `Map` inputs retain their keys. Both helpers accept promises, thenables, and plain values.

## Testing

Add runtime coverage for ordering, input types, object identity, callback behavior, early iteration exit, and termination. Add stdio and gRPC host tests for partial results across waits, plus a scenario snapshot verifying fulfilled and rejected records reach the model.

## Subscription

Organization-managed ChatGPT workspace. Multiple coworkers reproduce the same behavior.

## Model

GPT-5 Codex

## Platform

Darwin 25.6.0 arm64 arm
macOS 26.7.1 (25G241)

## Terminal

zsh on macOS

## Codex doctor report

Unavailable. Running `codex doctor` from the affected session itself attempts a network approval and fails with:

    network approval was cancelled before a decision was returned

`codex --version` also prints:

    WARNING: proceeding, even though we could not create PATH aliases: Operation not permitted (os error 1)

## What issue are you seeing?

A session launched explicitly with `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` still runs with an effective managed read-only permission profile and asks for approval when a command needs write or network access.

The user configuration also independently requests full autonomy:

    approval_policy = "never"
    sandbox_mode = "danger-full-access"

Despite both the startup flag and user configuration, the agent runtime reports an effective policy equivalent to:

    sandbox_mode = "read-only"
    permission_profile = "managed"
    network access = restricted

The agent cannot explain which managed requirement supplied that profile. Approval dialogs continue appearing, including for verification commands and `codex doctor`. This is happening to multiple coworkers, not one machine.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Configure Codex with `approval_policy = "never"` and `sandbox_mode = "danger-full-access"`.
2. Start a new session with:

       codex --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox

3. Ask Codex to perform a normal repository task that runs tests or another command requiring workspace writes or network access.
4. Observe that the session is assigned a managed read-only permission profile and produces an approval request.
5. Attempt `codex doctor`; observe that diagnostics are also blocked behind network approval.

No local configuration intentionally selects a read-only profile. The CLI currently provides no visible provenance explaining which system, cloud, MDM, or session layer overrode the explicit startup flag.

## Expected behavior

Either:

1. The explicit full-access flag takes effect, or
2. Codex refuses to start and clearly identifies the exact managed requirement that prohibited it.

Codex should not silently start with a materially different permission profile. The effective policy and its provenance should be visible before the first task, and `codex doctor` should remain usable for diagnosing this class of policy problem without requiring the blocked permission.

## Additional information

This may be an interaction between cloud-managed requirements, macOS managed preferences, or session/harness policy resolution. The main usability defect is that the effective `managed` read-only policy has no observable source, while the CLI appears to accept `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox`.

A useful fix would expose, in startup output and `codex doctor --json`, each effective approval/sandbox/permission-profile value together with the winning source layer and any rejected CLI override.

items.title: Feature request: reusable game-development primitives + MCP tooling for Codex

items.body:
## Summary

I'd like to suggest a reusable game-development layer for Codex: a curated, tested library of first-party game primitives and licensed placeholder assets, with an optional MCP/tooling interface that lets Codex retrieve, configure, validate, and extend those components.

The motivation is simple: coding agents repeatedly solve the same basic game-development problems. New-model demos and real user tasks frequently ask for things like a third-person character, vehicle physics, a camera, traffic AI, water, navigation, terrain, etc. Codex often has to generate and debug those systems again from scratch.

This is different from prompt caching. Prompt caching reuses model computation/context; this proposal would reuse **validated engineering work**.

## Proposed first-party primitives

Examples could include:

- Humanoid / third-person controller
- First-person controller
- Third- and first-person cameras
- Vehicle physics/controller
- Character animation controller
- Traffic and pedestrian AI
- Navigation/pathfinding
- Water/ocean system
- Terrain/open-world streaming
- Inventory/interaction primitives
- Common shaders/VFX
- Generic, properly licensed placeholder models, animations, textures, and sounds

These should be clean, tested OpenAI-maintained primitives rather than copies of previous users' generated games.

## MCP / tooling layer

MCP could provide the interface Codex uses to assemble and validate these primitives. For example:

- Create a tested third-person starter project
- Add/configure vehicle physics
- Add traffic/navigation
- Import licensed placeholder assets
- Run automated build/gameplay validation
- Upgrade or replace a primitive without rebuilding the project

Ideally the first-party library could work alongside an open interface so Unity, Unreal, Godot, Three.js, Blender, and third-party libraries could integrate with the same workflow.

Conceptually:

**Game primitive library = reusable validated engineering work**

**MCP = interface Codex uses to retrieve/configure/test/extend it**

A user-facing "Codex Games" or game-development workspace could eventually sit on top of those layers.

## Why this may matter economically

A lot of agent cost is not merely generating the initial source code. It is the repeated agent loop:

generate → run → fail → inspect → modify → run again.

Starting from known-good components could reduce model inference, sandbox/VM compute, build iterations, latency, and failure rates while allowing the model to spend more of its reasoning budget on the genuinely unique parts of a game.

For example, rather than building the thousandth generic open-world driving prototype from an empty directory, Codex could start from validated vehicle + humanoid + camera + traffic primitives and focus on the user's particular gameplay and design.

Training can teach a model *how* a vehicle controller works. This library would give the agent a tested vehicle controller it can immediately adapt.

## Scope

Both pieces are useful, but the main request is **(1) the curated/tested first-party component + asset library**. **(2) MCP/template/build-validation tooling** would be the automation and extensibility layer around it.

items.title: [Windows][App] Relaunch the desktop app automatically after an unexpected exit and resume interrupted chats
items.body:
### What variant of Codex are you using?

App (Windows, Microsoft Store ChatGPT/Codex desktop app)

### What feature would you like to see?

**Relaunch the desktop app automatically after an unexpected exit, and optionally resume the chats that were interrupted.**

**Problem**

On Windows the desktop app sometimes exits without any warning: crashes, silent exits with no Windows crash event, or being terminated by an unattended Store/AppX update. See for example #26807, #33197, #49059, #26395, and #33321 / #24047 for updates that never relaunch. Nothing brings the app back, so everything that runs inside it stops: in-progress turns and scheduled automations. The user only finds out when they next look at the machine. For unattended setups (automations running overnight, a work PC left running) this makes the app unreliable even when the crash itself is rare.

**Requested behavior**

1. **Auto-relaunch (opt-in setting).** If the main process ends unexpectedly (not because the user quit the app), start it again automatically after a short delay. Include crash-loop protection, for example stop after N restarts within M minutes and show a notification, so a launch-time crash does not loop forever. This should also cover the unattended-update case in #33321.
2. **Offer to resume interrupted work (opt-in).** After a relaunch, detect threads whose last turn was started but never completed, and offer to resume them (a prompt or a setting). Threads driven by automations and sub-agent threads would be skipped, since they restart by themselves and resuming them could run work twice.
3. **Say why it exited.** A small log entry or notification such as "ChatGPT exited unexpectedly at 03:12, restarted" would make the unattended case visible and would help with bug reports.

**Why built in**

An external tool can restart the process, but it has to guess about internal state: whether the user quit on purpose, which turns were really open, and whether a thread is already being written to. The app already has this information. It also avoids input simulation to resume chats.

**Related issues:** #24047 and #33321 (no relaunch after an update), #35801 (checkpointing and recovery after renderer reloads), #51082 (crash recovery loses active subagents).

### Additional information

Disclosure: I wrote a small unofficial community tool that does the restart-and-resume part from the outside on Windows, which is how I noticed what an external tool cannot know reliably: https://github.com/NickyVerslycken/ChatGPT-APP-watchdog. Happy to share logs or design notes if useful.

## Summary

Several issues (#50800, #50982, #51000, #49551) report delegated / Dot-created workers lacking tools that are available in manual chats. None of them identifies the provisioning mechanism the code actually contains: a **per-thread server signal** gates a background/delegated thread's tool catalog.

## The mechanism

In `codex-rs/tui/src/dynamic_tools.rs`:

- `request_thread_start_with_history_fallback` returns a per-thread `task_tools_available` bool (~L545),
- which flows through `register_background_thread` (~L1150) into `AppEvent::DynamicToolThreadStarted`.

So a native server (e.g. `codex_app`) can be **ready in one conversation while its tools are not supplied to a delegated/background thread** — "ready here, not supplied there" is a supported failure shape in the code, and it matches the observed symptom exactly: 9 of the 15 `mcp__codex_app__` tools are defined in the public repo (`dynamic_tools.rs`: `create_thread`, `send_message_to_thread`, `fork_thread`, `list_threads`/`list_archived_threads`, `read_thread`, `set_thread_title`, `set_thread_archived`, `wait_threads`), the tools exist, they just never reach the delegated worker.

## Observed instance (2026-10-05)

A fresh worker created through the supported desktop-task route executed with exit code 0 and *had* the native thread creation/read/send tools, while the older worker on the same machine lacked them — same computer, same app version, different per-thread provisioning outcome.

## Request

- Investigate whether the per-thread `task_tools_available` signal is gating tools incorrectly for delegated workers.
- Surface the mechanism in diagnostics so these failures are attributable instead of presenting as "tools missing."

## Related

#50800 (tool namespace disappears after session), #50982 (tools unavailable in dot-created tasks), #51000 (durable codex_app MCP startup fails), #49551 (delegated tasks lack tools manual chats have) — all symptoms; this issue names the mechanism.

## Summary

On the ChatGPT Windows desktop app, the access picker silently reverts from **Full Access** to **Custom** whenever the app updates (and on reloads). There is no notification. The user only discovers it when delegated workers start failing, or by manually inspecting the picker.

## Dated repro

- **2026-10-05 ~09:13 EDT:** Microsoft Store delivered a ~216 MB ChatGPT update (Windows package `26.930.4958.0`, replacing `26.930.3930.0`). After the update completed, the picker had reset to Custom. I manually restored it to Full Access — and the worker still reported `workspace-write` with `auto_review`, i.e. the UI change had not propagated to the worker's effective state at first check.
- The same silent reset has been observed on prior reloads/app updates, not just this one.

## Impact

- Delegated workers silently lose tool access after every update.
- Requested access (what the picker shows) diverges from effective access (what the worker reports) with no signal to the user.
- This is a recurring breakage vector: every Store update re-breaks previously working delegation setups.

## Expected

The picker selection should persist across app updates, or the app should explicitly notify the user when it changes the selection.

items.title: Feature: pluggable external browser provider for Browser Use (Safari/Orion/WebKit, etc.)

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
## Summary

Please make Codex Browser Use's browser backend configurable through a provider abstraction, rather than limiting browser automation to the bundled in-app browser and supported Chrome integration.

This is distinct from the existing **Open in external browser** preference for ordinary links. The request is for Browser Use / agent browser automation itself.

## Motivation

Codex Desktop can maintain a substantial bundled Chromium-derived browser runtime even when a user already has a preferred system browser. On memory-constrained machines (for example, 16 GB Apple Silicon Macs), running Codex's browser runtime alongside a normal browser and development stack can create avoidable memory pressure and swap usage.

Some users deliberately choose non-Chromium browsers such as Safari or Orion (WebKit) for lower resource usage, privacy, or platform integration. Browser Use currently cannot use those browsers as interchangeable backends.

A provider boundary would also decouple Codex's browser-agent API from a particular rendering engine.

## Proposed design

Expose a browser provider interface roughly along these lines:

- `builtin` — current bundled/in-app browser (default)
- `chrome` — existing Chrome integration
- `external` — user-configured browser/provider
- future providers: WebKit/Safari/Orion, Firefox, remote browser, custom automation bridge

Possible configuration:

```toml
[browser]
provider = "external"
executable = "/Applications/Orion.app/Contents/MacOS/Orion"
```

The exact configuration is not important; the important part is making Browser Use target a stable provider API.

A provider should expose a deterministic capability surface such as:

- enumerate/create/close tabs
- navigate
- current URL/title
- DOM/accessibility snapshot or equivalent semantic tree
- click/type/scroll
- screenshots
- permission/origin enforcement
- lifecycle/cleanup

If a browser cannot satisfy the required capabilities, Codex should report the unsupported capabilities rather than silently falling back.

## Resource-management benefit

This would allow users to avoid maintaining multiple heavyweight browser runtimes simultaneously and make Browser Use compatible with resource-optimized browser choices.

It would also allow Codex to keep the bundled browser as the secure, known-good default while advanced users explicitly opt into another provider.

## Security

External providers should remain subject to the same origin/network/approval policies as the bundled browser. Selecting an external provider should not bypass Codex permission enforcement.

## Related distinction

Existing UI/reporting already references **Open in external browser**, but that controls link opening rather than the Browser Use automation backend. This request is specifically for the latter.

A first implementation could expose the provider abstraction without promising arbitrary-browser support immediately; WebKit/Orion support could then be implemented independently against that interface.

The documented browser automation operation `locator.press('Control+c')` produces a DOM `copy` event without delivering any Ctrl/C `keydown` or `keyup` events. This reproduces on a plain textarea with document capture listeners, before involving a terminal library or application input handler. By comparison, `locator.press('Control+u')` delivers the normal ControlLeft and KeyU keydown/keyup sequence with `ctrlKey=true` and `metaKey=false`. The Copy-only delivery prevents an automated browser terminal from receiving Ctrl+C: it cannot cancel an edited shell line or interrupt a foreground command. Text, Tab, and Ctrl+U work. The same Copy-only result occurs with `ControlLeft+KeyC` and the native browser shortcut wrapper `tab.pressKey(null, 'ctrl+c')`. ### What steps can reproduce the bug? 1. );

```

```json
{"type":"copy","target":"native","prevented":false}
```

5. Send the comparison chord:

```js
await tab.playwright.getByLabel('Native key control').press('Control+u');
```

The retained event receipt contains all four key transitions:

```json
{"type":"keydown","target":"native","key":"Control","code":"ControlLeft","keyCode":17,"ctrl":true,"meta":false,"shift":false,"composing":false,"prevented":false}
{"type":"keydown","target":"native","key":"u","code":"KeyU","keyCode":85,"ctrl":true,"meta":false,"shift":false,"composing":false,"prevented":false}
{"type":"keyup","target":"native","key":"u","code":"KeyU","keyCode":85,"ctrl":true,"meta":false,"shift":false,"composing":false,"prevented":false}

codex-cli 0.160.0 (Homebrew cask), managed app-server daemon 0.160.0, macOS 27.0 (arm64)

### What issue are you seeing?

On 0.160.0, `codex --yolo` no longer gives **new** threads full access when the TUI runs on the managed app-server daemon. The thread is created with `approval_mode = on-request` and `sandbox_policy = {"type":"managed", file_system: restricted (cwd writable), "network":"restricted"}`. Commands that need network or local sockets fail (e.g. a local device bridge on `127.0.0.1:8710` → `Connect server failed`).

This is related to #49865 / #49088 (permissions lost after a daemon restart), but here the thread is **new**, not resumed:

1. `codex --yolo` started at 12:37:18. The thread was created at 12:37:19 **inside the long-running managed daemon process** (logs_2.sqlite shows it under the daemon's pid, not the TUI's), and `state_5.sqlite` records `approval_mode=on-request`, `sandbox_policy.type=managed`, `network=restricted`.
2. The same happens through a wrapper that starts its own app-server with `codex app-server -c approval_policy="never" -c sandbox_mode="danger-full-access" --listen unix://…` and then attaches `codex --remote unix://…`. The TUI (`client_name="codex-tui"`) creates the thread itself, and the thread ends up with `approval_mode=never` but `sandbox_policy` managed/restricted — the server-side `-c sandbox_mode="danger-full-access"` is not applied. Every `TurnInput` has `sandbox_policy: None, permission_profile: None`, so the restricted policy from thread creation sticks.
3. Additionally (= #49088/#49865): an older thread that had been running as `DangerFullAccess` on the daemon dropped to `WorkspaceWrite` after `codex app-server daemon restart`.

`~/.codex/config.toml` has no `sandbox_mode` / `approval_policy`. Before upgrading to 0.160.0 (from 0.159.2), `--yolo` in both setups gave full access.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. No `sandbox_mode`/`approval_policy` in `~/.codex/config.toml`; managed daemon running.
2. `codex --yolo`, start a new chat, ask it to run `curl -sI https://example.com` (or connect to any local TCP port).
3. Observe approval prompts / network denied; `select approval_mode, sandbox_policy from threads order by created_at desc limit 1` in `~/.codex/state_5.sqlite` shows on-request + managed/restricted.

### What is the expected behavior?

`--yolo` (and `-c sandbox_mode="danger-full-access"` on the app-server) should result in `approval_mode=never` + `danger-full-access` for threads created from that TUI, regardless of whether the TUI runs in-process, on the managed daemon, or via `--remote`.

### Additional information

Workaround: put `sandbox_mode = "danger-full-access"` and `approval_policy = "never"` in `~/.codex/config.toml` and restart the daemon.

items.title: [macOS desktop] GPT-6.1 Sol missing from model picker despite resolved CLI catalog and successful execution

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
### Summary

GPT-6.1 Sol is missing from the Codex Desktop model picker on macOS, even though the same machine/account can see the model in both the bundled and resolved Codex CLI catalogs and can successfully execute it directly through the CLI.

This looks like a Desktop UI/model-picker filtering issue rather than an account entitlement or backend availability issue.

### Environment

- Platform: macOS, Apple Silicon
- Codex CLI: `0.160.0`
- Codex Desktop: latest available app version as of 2026-10-05 (exact build number not captured)
- Authentication: ChatGPT account

The same ChatGPT account had previously been able to use GPT-6.1 Sol on another device.

### Observed behavior

In Codex Desktop on macOS, the model picker shows models such as:

- GPT-6 Astra
- GPT-6 Sol
- GPT-6 Luna
- GPT-5.6 Sol
- GPT-5.6 Terra
- GPT-5.6 Luna

but GPT-6.1 Sol is absent.

### Diagnostic evidence

The model exists in the bundled catalog:

```bash
codex debug models --bundled 2>&1 | grep -q 'gpt-6\.1-sol'
```

Result:

```text
BUNDLED: GPT-6.1 Sol FOUND
```

The model also exists in the resolved/available CLI catalog:

```bash
codex debug models 2>&1 | grep -q 'gpt-6\.1-sol'
```

Result:

```text
AVAILABLE: GPT-6.1 Sol FOUND
```

Most importantly, direct execution succeeds:

```bash
codex exec --model gpt-6.1-sol \
  --sandbox read-only \
  --ephemeral \
  --skip-git-repo-check \
  --color never \
  'Reply with exactly: OK'
```

Relevant output:

```text
OpenAI Codex v0.160.0
model: gpt-6.1-sol
provider: openai
reasoning effort: high
...
codex
OK
```

So the backend accepts the model for this account and the CLI can run it successfully, while the Desktop picker still omits it.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Sign in to Codex Desktop on macOS with an account that has access to GPT-6.1 Sol.
2. Open the model picker and observe that GPT-6.1 Sol is missing.
3. Install/use Codex CLI `0.160.0` with the same account.
4. Run `codex debug models --bundled` and confirm `gpt-6.1-sol` is present.
5. Run `codex debug models` and confirm `gpt-6.1-sol` is present in the resolved catalog.
6. Run `codex exec --model gpt-6.1-sol ...` and observe successful execution.

### Expected behavior

If GPT-6.1 Sol is present in the resolved model catalog and the backend accepts direct execution for the current account, Codex Desktop should expose GPT-6.1 Sol in the model picker as well.

### Actual behavior

GPT-6.1 Sol works through Codex CLI but is not shown in the Codex Desktop model picker on the same Mac/account.

### Related issue

Possibly related to #51024, but the diagnostic boundary is different: in #51024 the resolved local catalog reportedly excludes `gpt-6.1-sol`, while in this case the resolved catalog includes it and direct execution succeeds.

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app

items.body:
The ChatGPT desktop app for Windows (Store package OpenAI.Codex 26.930.6422.0) downloads runtime bundle 26.909.12148 to `%USERPROFILE%\.cache\codex-runtimes\codex-primary-runtime`. After the cache was cleared on 5 October 2026, the app downloaded the same bundle again.

The bundle contains:
- Python 3.12.14 (`dependencies\python`). Python 3.12.15 was released on 30 September 2026.
- OpenSSL 3.5.5 in the bundled Git (`dependencies\native\git\mingw64\bin`). OpenSSL 3.5.9 is the current 3.5 release.
- OpenSSL 3.6.4 in poppler (`dependencies\native\poppler\Library\bin`). OpenSSL 3.6.5 is current, and the 3.6 series reaches end of life on 1 November 2026.

Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management flags the Python and Git OpenSSL files with CVEs rated CVSS 7 or above, up to 9.8. Organisations that need a clean vulnerability scan (for example UK Cyber Essentials Plus) cannot keep the app installed. Please ship a runtime bundle with current Python 3.12 and OpenSSL 3.5, and a supported OpenSSL in poppler, and say when it will reach users.

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: auth
labels.description: Issues related to authentication and accounts

labels.description: Issues related to the use of model context protocol (MCP) servers

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

items.body:
### What variant of Codex are you using?

Codex CLI 0.159.2 on macOS. Tested with isolated temporary `CODEX_HOME` directories and local marketplaces.

### What feature would you like to see?

Provide a supported way to bundle a pre-registered MCP OAuth client ID, requested scopes, and a fixed callback port in a portable Agent Plugins package. This could be a standardized schema extension or a documented Codex-specific extension, rather than allowing arbitrary unknown fields.

The existing Codex compatibility format can declare these settings in `.mcp.json`, but migrating to root `plugin.json` / `mcp.json` currently loses them. This prevents distributing a self-contained plugin for an enterprise MCP service that requires a pre-registered public client and an approved loopback callback port, without asking every user to edit separate configuration.

This is a packaging feature gap, not a report that MCP OAuth itself is unsupported. The portable v1 schema explicitly disallows these fields, and Codex's portable parser enforces that schema. Please also make the resulting server omission actionable in installation/list diagnostics.

### Additional information

#### Minimal local reproduction

Create a marketplace containing `plugins/oauth-example/` and these files. The example endpoint and client ID are placeholders; no reachable MCP server, credentials, or network access to an MCP endpoint is needed to reproduce configuration loading.

`plugins/oauth-example/plugin.json`:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://agent-plugins.org/schemas/1.0.0/plugin.schema.json",
  "name": "oauth-example",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "description": "Portable OAuth configuration reproduction"
}
```

`plugins/oauth-example/mcp.json`:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://agent-plugins.org/schemas/1.0.0/mcp.schema.json",
  "mcpServers": {
    "example": {
      "type": "streamable-http",
      "url": "https://mcp.example.com/mcp",
      "scopes": ["openid", "offline_access", "example.read"],
      "oauth": {
        "clientId": "example-public-client",
        "callbackPort": 38000
      }
    }
  }
}
```

`.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` at the marketplace root:

```json
{
  "name": "oauth-repro",
  "plugins": [
    {
      "name": "oauth-example",
      "source": {
        "source": "local",
        "path": "./plugins/oauth-example"
      },
      "policy": {
        "installation": "AVAILABLE",
        "authentication": "ON_INSTALL"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

In an isolated Codex home:

```sh
export CODEX_HOME="$(mktemp -d)"
codex plugin marketplace add /absolute/path/to/marketplace
codex plugin add oauth-example@oauth-repro
codex mcp list --json
```

Observed on 0.159.2:

- Marketplace registration and plugin installation exit successfully.
- `codex mcp list --json` exits successfully and returns `[]`; its captured stdout/stderr did not explain the invalid server fields.
- Control: removing `oauth` and `scopes` from the installed portable MCP configuration makes the `example` HTTP server appear in `codex mcp list --json`.
- The URL-only control no longer bundles the required OAuth client/scopes/callback settings. This test concerns local configuration loading, not successful authentication against the placeholder endpoint.

In a separate migration check, keeping a `.codex-plugin/plugin.json` referencing `.mcp.json` alongside the portable manifest did not restore these settings. The portable manifest selects root `mcp.json`, and the compatibility overlay does not override portable MCP paths.

#### Desired outcome

- A documented packaging mechanism preserves the public client ID, requested scopes, and fixed callback port without a helper executable or per-user config edits.
- The same stable plugin/server identity can be retained when migrating from the supported compatibility layout.
- Until supported, installation/list output should identify the rejected server and unsupported fields, rather than showing only an empty inventory.

References:

- [Portable MCP schema](https://agent-plugins.org/schemas/1.0.0/mcp.schema.json): HTTP entries allow only `type`, `url`, and optional `headers`, with `additionalProperties: false`.
- [Codex portable MCP parser](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/codex-mcp/src/agent_plugin_config.rs): `AgentPluginMcpServer` uses `deny_unknown_fields`.
- [Codex portable manifest handling](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/core-plugins/src/agent_plugin_manifest.rs): portable MCP path defaults to `./mcp.json`; the OpenAI extension/compatibility overlay does not replace it.
- [Packaging documentation](https://developers.openai.com/plugins/build/plugins).
- Related umbrella issue: #35006 tracks enterprise OAuth lifecycle reliability; this request concerns portable package configuration, not refresh or reauthentication lifecycle.
