For roughly the last month, my Codex 5-hour usage limit has been draining dramatically faster than before, to the point where I can now complete only a small fraction of the coding work I used to be able to do within the same allowance.

This does not appear to be caused by a specific model, repository, VS Code extension, or coding workload. I can reproduce it in the standalone Codex CLI with a trivial prompt and no tools.

Environment:
- Windows
- ChatGPT Plus
- Codex CLI 0.160.0
- Standalone CLI / codex-tui
- Fresh/simple session
- No repository analysis
- No file reads
- No shell commands
- No build/test tools

Minimal reproduction:

I repeatedly sent:

`Say hello`

18 times.

According to the local Codex JSONL session log, those 18 trivial turns resulted in:

- 287,074 input tokens
- 276,352 cached input tokens
- 10,722 non-cached input tokens
- 161 output tokens
- approximately 96.3% cache hit rate
- 5h server-side usage increasing from 49% to 52%
- 7d usage remaining at 55%

The input per turn stayed roughly stable, around 15.8k–16.1k tokens, so this does not appear to be caused by runaway context growth. The conversation history only increased the prompt size slightly from turn to turn.

The 5h usage values are not inferred from the UI. They come directly from the server-side values stored in the local JSONL log under:

`payload.rate_limits.primary.used_percent`

The relevant session ID is:

`01a10be3-c7ac-7dc3-91a7-cfb0597d4841`

What is especially concerning is that almost all of the input was cached, yet the 5h allowance still increased by about 3 percentage points for a workload that produced only 161 output tokens and performed no useful coding work.

I also tested lighter models, including GPT-5.5 Light, and the abnormal drain remained. Therefore this does not appear to be specific to GPT-5.6 Sol.

I initially suspected the VS Code extension because I had previously seen the same behavior there, but the standalone CLI reproduces it as well, so the problem does not appear to be limited to the VS Code bundled runtime.

In real coding sessions, one user request can generate many model/tool/model iterations, so this behavior becomes much more severe. In practice, my Codex allowance now disappears dramatically faster than it did about a month ago, even though my workflow has not changed significantly.

I also have older Codex session logs from August and September. Comparing them with recent sessions shows that the relationship between processed tokens and 5h quota usage has become substantially worse over time. Earlier sessions often processed significantly larger contexts while consuming the rate limit much more slowly.

This looks less like a normal context-size issue and more like a possible regression or change in server-side quota accounting / request weighting. Possible areas worth checking include:

- cached input token weighting
- per-request or per-agent-step quota accounting
- changes in how repeated agent/model calls are charged against the 5h allowance
- account-level metering regressions

Expected behavior:

A trivial, heavily cached prompt with no tools, no repository analysis, no reasoning-heavy task, and only a few output tokens should not consume the 5h allowance at this rate.

Actual behavior:

Even repeated trivial prompts consume several percentage points of the 5h allowance, while real programming tasks drain the allowance extremely quickly.

Could the Codex team inspect the backend metering for the session ID above and confirm whether this quota consumption is expected? I can provide the complete JSONL session log and older session logs for comparison if needed.

items.title: [macOS] Archived-thread resume loop (~37 failures/s) precedes recurring CrBrowserMain SIGTRAP crashes
items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

Three retained macOS crash reports identify:
- `26.928.21956` (build `12404`) — October 1, 2026
- `26.928.31416` (build `12553`) — October 4, 2026
- `26.930.31730` (build `12947`) — October 5, 2026

The currently installed/running version is `26.930.51102` (build `13100`), following an update on October 5. The repeated crash described below was observed on the three earlier versions; recurrence on build 13100 is not confirmed.

### What subscription do you have?

Not included in this report. The evidence concerns a desktop main-process crash and local archived-thread recovery.

### What platform is your computer?

macOS 26.5.1 (25F80), ARM64 native. Bundle identifier: `com.openai.codex`; executable name: `ChatGPT`.

### What issue are you seeing?

The desktop application has repeatedly terminated unexpectedly. All three retained crash reports show `EXC_BREAKPOINT / SIGTRAP` on `CrBrowserMain` (`com.apple.main-thread`), with the same Codex Framework binary and the same top two image offsets.

A particularly consistent precursor is a high-frequency recovery loop for **the same already-archived local thread**. The app repeatedly reads the thread/config, attempts `thread/resume`, receives `-32600` / `thread_archived`, reports failed hydration, and immediately starts recovery again. The affected thread remains archived in local thread metadata. It is not the current active thread.

Counts below are from the retained rotating main-process logs, not the entire process lifetime:

| Crash date | Archived-thread resume failures | Observed failure rate |
|---|---:|---:|
| October 1 | 11,323 | ~37.3/s |
| October 4 | 12,735 | ~22.8/s |
| October 5 | 13,220 | ~36.9/s |

For October 5, the retained log window runs from `07:29:01.430Z` through `07:34:59.837Z`, immediately before the crash captured at `07:35:00.212Z`. In that roughly six-minute window, the main-process logs contain 119,074 lines / 50,927,907 bytes.

Sanitized recurring sequence:

```text
thread/read
config/read
browser_use_runtime_paths_selected
thread/resume -> errorCode=-32600
Request failed failureReason=thread_archived
  message="session <ARCHIVED_THREAD> is archived"
VM lifecycle vmEvent=thread_resume_failed
thread_hydration outcome=failure reason=hydration_failed
query-cache-invalidate
maybe_resume_started
  previousResumeState=needs_resume
  documentVisibilityState=hidden
  rendererWindowFocused=false
# repeats for the same archived thread
```

The three crash reports share:

```text
Exception: EXC_BREAKPOINT
Signal: SIGTRAP
Termination: SIGNAL / Code 5 / Trace/BPT trap: 5
Faulting thread: CrBrowserMain / com.apple.main-thread
Codex Framework: 154.0.8037.57
Framework UUID: 4c4c4449-5555-3144-a137-5e9c1e5750c3
Top frame imageOffset: 4702680
Second frame imageOffset: 3333080
Additional frames include:
  v8::ObjectTemplate::NewInstance(v8::Local<v8::Context>)
  v8::FunctionTemplate::New(...)
```

Some symbols have large symbol offsets in the stripped framework, so these names should not be treated as a precise source-level assertion diagnosis.

The retry loop is a strongly correlated potential trigger, **not a proven causal explanation for the V8 trap**. The crash reports do not explicitly identify an out-of-memory termination; that does not exclude memory pressure as a contributing factor.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

There is no deliberately verified minimal reproduction yet. The observed pattern is:

1. Use the macOS desktop application with an existing local thread that has already been archived.
2. Some persisted client references to that archived thread remain. Read-only inspection found two paused queued follow-ups with an archived-session rejection, a pending project-assignment reference, and a managed-worktree archive reference. Which reference causes the retry loop is unconfirmed.
3. During normal use, the client repeatedly attempts to resume that same archived thread, even though the backend consistently rejects it.
4. The loop continues at tens of failures per second, followed by an unexpected desktop main-process exit with the shared signature above.

The app was not intentionally crashed or subjected to a new stress test during diagnosis. These observations come from existing crash reports and logs. Thread identifiers, titles, account details, and local project paths have been redacted.

### What is the expected behavior?

An archived-thread rejection should be treated as a terminal recovery outcome until an explicit user action changes the thread state. Hydration/cache invalidation should not immediately reissue the same resume operation indefinitely.

The client should clear or pause stale recovery references, bound retries/back off for recoverable errors, and keep unrelated active threads and the main process stable.

### Additional information

- After build 13100 launched, approximately one hour of observed main-process logs showed no `thread_archived` failures. This short observation does not prove the issue is fixed.
- A separate October 5 exit/relaunch had explicit Sparkle `install_started`, successful download, transport shutdown, and a subsequent build-13100 startup. That update restart is not being counted as one of the crashes.
- Existing reports #49730 and #41618 describe desktop SIGTRAP crashes, but the exact archived-thread retry-loop precursor and shared offsets reported here were not established in those reports.
- This submission contains a sanitized diagnostic summary only. No session transcripts, prompts, global-state file, credentials, full raw logs, or complete crash reports are attached.

Please investigate terminal handling of `thread_archived` in hydration/resume/cache invalidation and whether the sustained loop can exhaust or invalidate native V8 resources.

### What issue are you seeing?

## Summary

When using `qwen3.6:35b-a3b` through Ollama in the Codex App on macOS, the model correctly decides to use tools, but Codex sometimes renders the intended tool invocation as literal text instead of executing it.

The same model produces valid structured tool calls when tested directly against both Ollama's native `/api/chat` API and its OpenAI-compatible `/v1/responses` API.

This appears to be specific to the Codex App / local-provider tool integration.

## Environment

- OS: macOS, Apple Silicon
- Codex App version: **26.930.51102**
- Ollama version: **0.35.1**
- Model: `qwen3.6:35b-a3b`
- Provider: Ollama
- Integration: Ollama GUI → Apps → Codex / ChatGPT Codex App

## Issue

For example, I asked the model to inspect a local repository.

The model correctly responded:

```text
I'll start by inspecting the full repository structure and then reading every source file.
```

But instead of Codex executing the intended tool call, the UI displayed a literal tool invocation such as:

```text
<tool_code_interpreter>code_interpreter(code="import os

cwd = '/Users/user/project'
for root, dirs, files in os.walk(cwd):
    ...
", runtime="python")
```

The turn then ended rather than executing the tool.

In another attempt, after explicitly steering the model toward shell execution, the Codex App displayed calls such as:

```text
exec(
  command=["find", ".", "-not", "-path", "./.git*", "-not", "-name", ".DS_Store"],
  sandbox_permissions="allow",
  justification="List project files for inspection"
)
```

and:

```text
exec(
  command=["ls", "-R"],
  sandbox_permissions="allow",
  justification="List project directory structure"
)
```

The model clearly understands that it should invoke Codex tools, but the tool invocation is not reliably being dispatched as an actual tool call.

## Direct Ollama tool calling works

I tested the exact same model directly through Ollama.

### `/api/chat`

Requesting a `list_files` function produces a valid structured tool call:

```json
{
  "message": {
    "role": "assistant",
    "content": "",
    "tool_calls": [
      {
        "id": "call_example",
        "function": {
          "index": 0,
          "name": "list_files",
          "arguments": {
            "path": "."
          }
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

So native Ollama tool calling works with `qwen3.6:35b-a3b`.

### `/v1/responses`

I also tested Ollama's OpenAI-compatible Responses API directly.

It returned:

```json
{
  "type": "function_call",
  "status": "completed",
  "call_id": "call_example",
  "name": "list_files",
  "arguments": "{\"path\":\".\"}"
}
```

Therefore:

- Qwen3.6 is capable of generating the tool call.
- Ollama `/api/chat` parses it correctly.
- Ollama `/v1/responses` converts it into a valid Responses API `function_call`.
- The failure occurs when using the model through the Codex App.

## Minimal reproduction

1. Install/run Ollama.
2. Pull:

```bash
ollama pull qwen3.6:35b-a3b
```

3. Enable/use the model in Codex App through the Ollama Apps integration.
4. Open any local repository in Codex.
5. Ask:

```text
Use the shell execution tool.

Run exactly one command:

pwd

Do not run any other command.
After the tool returns, tell me the exact output.
```

Or ask Codex to inspect the repository.

### Expected behavior

Codex should receive a structured tool call from the local model, execute the shell/filesystem/code tool, pass the result back to the model, and continue the turn.

### Actual behavior

The local model may emit a textual representation of the intended tool invocation, for example:

```text
<tool_code_interpreter>...
```

or:

```text
exec(command=[...])
```

instead of Codex dispatching it as an executable tool call.

The turn may then end without the requested operation being completed.

## Additional verification

Plain model generation works normally:

```bash
ollama run qwen3.6:35b-a3b
```

When instructed not to use tools, the model produces a complete normal response.

This therefore does not appear to be a basic inference/model-loading problem.

It specifically appears when Codex App tool execution is involved.

## Why this may be a Codex integration issue

A simple function tool works correctly through Ollama's `/v1/responses` endpoint, so the basic Responses API function-call conversion appears functional.

The issue may involve how Codex-specific tools such as code interpreter / shell execution are represented to local Responses API providers, or how Codex App handles returned calls from a non-OpenAI model.

There appears to be a related issue:

- #38490 — local Ollama models fail to call MCP tools while the same MCP setup works with GPT-5.6.

My case appears broader because it occurs with Codex's built-in execution/tool path rather than only MCP tools.

## Logs / screenshots

I can provide:

- screenshots of the Codex UI showing literal `<tool_code_interpreter>` / `exec(...)` output
- the full successful `/api/chat` response
- the full successful `/v1/responses` response
- Codex App version
- Ollama version
- additional logs if there is a recommended diagnostic procedure

1. Install and run Ollama on macOS.

2. Pull the model:

```bash
ollama pull qwen3.6:35b-a3b
```

3. In the Ollama GUI, enable the Codex / ChatGPT integration so the local model is available in the Codex App.

4. Open the Codex App and select:

```text
qwen3.6:35b-a3b
```

5. Open any local project/repository.

6. Ask the model to execute a simple shell command, for example:

```text
Use the shell execution tool.

Run exactly one command:

pwd

Do not run any other command.
After the tool returns, tell me the exact output.
```

7. Observe that instead of executing the tool normally, Codex may display the intended tool invocation literally, for example:

```text
exec(command=["pwd"], ...)
```

or:

```text
<tool_code_interpreter>...
```

The turn may then end without the command actually being executed.

The same model successfully produces structured tool calls when tested directly against Ollama's `/api/chat` and `/v1/responses` endpoints.

macOS **27.0.1**, Apple Silicon.

### What issue are you seeing?

**Settings > Connections > Control this Mac > Allow connections** cannot be enabled. The toggle remains off. Remote previously allowed me to open and continue existing desktop chats from my phone. That workflow is now blocked.

The latest toast is:

```text
Could not enable remote control. Please ensure only one instance of ChatGPT is running
```

Earlier attempts showed:

```text
Couldn't update remote control availability
```

Opening existing desktop chats from the phone also produced:

```text
Another Codex session is using this task. Finish and close that session, then try again.
```

The failure has been observed repeatedly during troubleshooting from September 30 through October 5, 2026. This report concerns one affected installation. It does not establish a service-wide outage or a confirmed root cause.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

On the affected installation:

1. Keep the ChatGPT desktop app open with existing local Codex chats.
2. Open **Settings > Connections > Control this Mac**.
3. Try to enable **Allow connections**.
4. Observe that the toggle remains off and the already-running-instance toast appears.
5. Attempt to open the existing desktop chats through the previously working phone Remote connection. The chats cannot be continued.

This is a repeatable UI failure on this installation. A deterministic clean-profile reproducer for the underlying ownership collision has not been established.

### What is the expected behavior?

Allow connections should enable Remote for the desktop backend that owns the existing chats. The phone should be able to continue those chats without closing the desktop session.

Internal automation helpers should not implicitly compete with the desktop backend for the same host's Remote registration. If another backend owns the registration, the UI should identify that condition and offer a supported repair or handoff instead of suggesting that a second visible ChatGPT app is open.

### Additional information

**Observed evidence**

- A fresh process check found exactly **one main ChatGPT desktop process**.
- Earlier Remote connection diagnostics captured `HTTP 409 Conflict` with `{"detail":"Remote app server already online"}`.
- The default local app-server control socket currently reports `connected`, but its complete loaded-thread list does **not** contain the active desktop chat performing this investigation. Connectivity at that socket therefore does not establish that the desktop backend is reachable remotely.
- The latest read-only diagnostic on October 5 returned:

```json
  "diagnosticChatLoaded": false,
  "environmentIdMatchesDesktopSavedState": true,
  "installationIdMatchesDesktopSavedState": true,
  "rpcFailure": null
}
```

The exact helper that holds the conflicting registration has **not** been identified. This is a hypothesis supported by the launch behavior, not a confirmed attribution of the 409 to a particular process.

A third-party tunnel connector also launched a Codex app-server in this environment. It was initially observed connected to Remote with zero loaded chats.
```
$ codex sandbox -- /bin/true
bwrap: Can't mkdir parents for /run/host/var/lib/containers/storage/overlay/<id>/merged/tmp/codex-daemon-1000: Permission denied
```

The TUI fails the same way at `thread/start` ("failed to load AGENTS.md instructions").

`/tmp`'s tmpfs is mounted three times; distrobox bind-mounts the host's `/` read-only at `/run/host`:
```
/tmp
/run/host/tmp                                              # reachable; masked OK
/run/host/var/lib/containers/storage/overlay/<id>/merged/tmp   # container's own rootfs seen via host
```

```
sudo unshare -m --propagation private sh -c "umount -l /run/host/var/lib/containers/storage/overlay/<id>/merged/tmp; setpriv --reuid=1000 --regid=1000 --init-groups env HOME=$HOME PATH=$PATH codex sandbox -- /bin/echo OK"
OK
```

Related: #47674, #48758, #47455.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Create a distrobox container on rootful Podman (I use Bazzite; any host where `/var/lib/containers/storage/overlay` is `drwx------ root` should work):
   ```
   distrobox create --root --name cx --image docker.io/library/archlinux:latest
   distrobox enter --root cx
   ```
2. Inside the box, install Codex 0.160.0 (`sudo pacman -S openai-codex`, or npm).
3. Run any sandboxed command:
   ```
   codex sandbox -- /bin/true
   ```
   **Actual:** `bwrap: Can't mkdir parents for /run/host/var/lib/containers/storage/overlay/<id>/merged/tmp/codex-daemon-<uid>: Permission denied`, exit 1. Starting the TUI fails the same way at `thread/start`.
   **Expected:** exits 0.
4. Why: `/tmp`'s filesystem is also reachable under `/run/host`, once through a root-only directory:
   ```
   $ awk '$5 ~ /tmp$/ {print $3, $5}' /proc/self/mountinfo
   0:58 /tmp
   ```

Ignore stale refresh responses in agents overview tests

Aborting a refresh task cannot retract a response already queued for delivery. The test helper could consume that stale response and return before the replacement refresh completed.

### What issue are you seeing?

An explicitly approved repository-instruction migration became a sequence of separate permission interruptions for related Git operations. The project files were writable, but the effective managed permission profile made the repository's `.git` directory read-only. Working in an isolated Git worktree still required writes to the primary repository's Git metadata.

The user repeatedly had to return to approval prompts during worktree setup, staging/committing, and publication/bookkeeping. The agent also fragmented the work into too many separately approved operations, compounding the problem. This report concerns approval granularity and the resulting workflow, not a claim that every individual sandbox check was incorrect.

Impact: a small, authorised change required sustained human supervision. The user reports that reading and responding to permission prompts accounted for much of the waiting. No exact prompt count or timing breakdown was measured.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Observed workflow; not yet a clean, deterministic reproduction:

1. Use a managed `workspace-write` session with the project directory writable and its `.git` directory explicitly read-only.
2. Ask the agent to migrate shared repository instructions and explicitly authorise the work.
3. Follow project rules requiring an isolated Git worktree and staged Git lifecycle operations.
4. Approve required Git operations as the task progresses.
5. Observe additional prompts for related operations in the same task, requiring the user to repeatedly interrupt other work.

The operation classes included worktree creation, staging, commits and pushes. Publication can appropriately have a separate approval boundary; the concern is repeated fragmentation across the overall approved workflow. Third-party project instructions required additional tracking and review operations, so this is not asserted to reproduce in stock Codex without those instructions.

### What is the expected behavior?

Provide a narrow, explicit task-duration authorisation covering the intended worktree and necessary Git metadata operations, with the scope and remaining approval boundaries visible up front. Keep destructive actions, unrelated repositories, hook/config changes and external publication separately controlled as appropriate.

The agent should batch related operations where practical. The UI should distinguish time executing from time waiting for approval, so users can understand where the delay occurs. This is not a request to make natural-language approval silently override the sandbox or to disable safeguards.

- Effective session profile: managed, restricted filesystem, workspace-write, project `.git` read-only, restricted network.
- Third-party Consciousness plugin and custom project/global instructions were active; their workflow requirements contributed to the number of Git operations.
- Session identifier: `01a10acf-8da5-7e01-9fe6-06486fe376df`. Included with the user's permission for correlation; it is not a public transcript URL or a feedback-upload receipt.
- Transcript, raw logs, private repository paths and project contents are deliberately omitted.
- Related reports: #37827 (parallel-session approval overhead), #24115 (managed Git permissions), #49078 (permission profile on resume). items.body:
Same Codex version and ChatGPT account:

Windows:
account/read -> 0.422s -> success

WSL2:
account/read -> 15.016s -> -32603
"workspace routing discovery timed out"

Control:
codex exec -> succeeds on both Windows and WSL2

### What version of Codex CLI is running?

0.160.0 on both Windows and WSL2.

### What subscription do you have?

Not provided.

### Which model were you using?

No model turn was started for the account/read reproduction. The read-only exec control used each platform's configured default model (gpt-6-luna on Windows and gpt-6.1-sol on WSL2).

### What platform is your computer?

- Windows 11 x64
- WSL2 Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS, x86_64, kernel 6.18.40.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2

### What terminal emulator and version are you using (if applicable)?

PowerShell on Windows and an Ubuntu shell in WSL2. The minimal app-server reproduction below communicates over stdin/stdout and does not depend on terminal UI behavior.

### Codex doctor report

Not attached. The app-server account/read reproduction is sufficient to show the failure and avoids publishing unrelated local configuration details.

### What issue are you seeing?

With the same Codex 0.160.0 version and ChatGPT account, a minimal app-server `account/read` request succeeds on Windows but times out on WSL2 after approximately 15 seconds. The WSL2 response is:

```json
{"id":2,"error":{"code":-32603,"message":"workspace routing discovery timed out"}}
```

A read-only `codex exec` control succeeds on both platforms and returns `CODEX_WSL_OK`. The WSL2 run also logs model-catalog refresh timeouts and MCP transport failures, but inference itself succeeds.

The timeout does not identify which internal stage consumed the deadline. The source constructs an `accounts/check` discovery request, but the runtime evidence does not establish that this request is the stage that stalled.

Direct TUI testing also succeeded on Windows and failed during bootstrap on WSL2 with the same routing-timeout error.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

On each platform, start that platform's native Codex 0.160.0 app-server executable with its existing ChatGPT login. Send these newline-delimited JSON messages to stdin:

1. Initialize:

```json
{"id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"clientInfo":{"name":"routing_repro","version":"1.0"},"capabilities":{"experimentalApi":true}}}
```

2. After receiving the response to request 1, send:

```json
{"method":"initialized","params":{}}
{"id":2,"method":"account/read","params":{"refreshToken":false}}
```

3. Measure the time from sending request 2 until its response. No thread or turn is needed.

Observed results:

- Windows: 0.422 seconds; success; `workspaceRouting` present.
- WSL2 Ubuntu: 15.016 seconds; JSON-RPC -32603, `workspace routing discovery timed out`.

Then run this read-only inference control on each platform:

```sh
codex exec --skip-git-repo-check --sandbox read-only "Do not access or change any files. Reply with exactly: CODEX_WSL_OK"
```

Both platforms returned `CODEX_WSL_OK` and exit 0.

### What is the expected behavior?

With a valid ChatGPT login, `account/read` should complete on WSL2 as it does on Windows, or provide a diagnostic that identifies the stage that timed out. The read-only inference control should continue to work independently of account/workspace initialization.

### Additional information

Network checks performed previously found matching ChatGPT DNS A records, verified TLS and IPv4 TCP connectivity from WSL2, and no configured proxy environment variables on either side. An unauthenticated GET to `/backend-api/wham/accounts/check` returned 401 on both Windows and WSL2; this does not test Codex's authenticated request and does not identify the cause. No TLS verification or security controls were disabled.

Source review of rust-v0.160.0 shows that app-server wraps the complete account read in a 15-second Tokio timeout, including config loading, waiting, and HTTP work. The measured error alone does not prove that an authenticated `accounts/check` request was reached or stalled.

Related reports:

- #49827 — app-server routing failure while `codex exec` succeeds (0.159.2, Windows).
- #50211 — TUI account/read routing failure (0.160.0, macOS).
- #48600 — similar Windows/WSL TUI timeout report; closed as a duplicate of #47145. Its reported `log_dir` behavior differs from this minimal Windows-success/WSL2-failure app-server comparison.

No tokens, account IDs, email addresses, session IDs, auth.json contents, or user-specific paths are included.

`invalid turn/start params: AbsolutePathBuf deserialized without a base path`

- Running Windows package: 26.930.3930.0

- Chrome and Computer Use plugin packages: 26.930.31730, enabled (browser extension version not independently verified)

2. User opens that delegated conversation and sends a follow-up in desktop UI.
3. A red error banner appears; the turn does not start.
4. An ordinary new local-project conversation with the correct native Windows working directory runs commands and CUA successfully.

This is an observed workflow, not a clean-install minimal reproduction. Restarting did not consistently resolve the symptoms.

Application logs on 2026-10-05 show turn/start error -32602 at approximately 06:05 UTC and at 07:12:12, 07:12:19, 07:12:27, and 07:12:53 UTC.

`/tmp/<redacted>/workspace/C:\Users\<redacted>\...\task-2`

- #28094: Windows/WSL path handling.
- #49458: dot-created Windows tasks lack Computer Use while ordinary local sessions work. Similar tool-availability variation was observed here, but its relationship to this path error is unconfirmed.

A separate delegated-action approval issue was observed; it is not being attributed to this path parsing failure.

items.body:
### What version of the Codex IDE extension are you using?

`openai.chatgpt 26.930.51102`

### Which IDE and platform are you using?

- VS Code
- Linux x64
- Two VS Code windows with the Codex extension active

### What issue are you seeing?

The Codex Output channel repeatedly records batches of `fs/getMetadata` requests as errors:

```text
[error] Request failed conversationId=none durationMs=18 error={"code":-32603,"message":"No such file or directory (os error 2)"} failureReason=null method=fs/getMetadata pendingCountAfter=9 priority=interactive queueWaitMs=0 source=filesystem timeoutMs=0
[error] Request failed conversationId=none durationMs=46 error={"code":-32603,"message":"No such file or directory (os error 2)"} failureReason=null method=fs/getMetadata pendingCountAfter=4 priority=interactive queueWaitMs=18 source=filesystem timeoutMs=0
```

Request IDs and local timestamps have been omitted. The complete logs are not attached because they contain account identifiers, conversation identifiers, and local paths.

In one session, the two Codex logs contained 440 and 88 matching records respectively. The requests occur in short batches, commonly immediately after a turn starts or cross-window thread state is refreshed. They complete in milliseconds, have `conversationId=none`, and do not cause a visible turn, attachment, or preview failure.

Inspection of the installed extension bundle indicates that these requests are made by the HTML visualization/artifact snapshot path. That code examines optional Codex workspace, writable, and temporary visualization roots. Its metadata-probe helpers explicitly catch the not-found error and return an empty result/null, so ENOENT appears to be an anticipated condition at the caller even though the generic request layer has already emitted an `[error]` record.

The logged record does not include the requested path, so users cannot distinguish an expected missing optional path from an actionable missing file.

This report is specifically about error-level logging of a handled condition. Existing issues mentioning the same line appear to concern dropped or queued messages; no such functional failure was observed here.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the Codex extension in VS Code on Linux.
2. Open two VS Code windows with Codex active.
3. Start or continue a turn in one window.
4. Watch **Output → Codex** in the other window.
5. Observe a cross-window thread-state broadcast followed by a batch of `fs/getMetadata` ENOENT errors.

The errors can also occur during other thread refreshes; two windows appear to increase their frequency.

### Expected behavior

An anticipated missing optional artifact/snapshot path should either:

- be treated as a normal negative metadata result without error-level logging, or
- be logged only at debug/trace level.

If the failure is unexpected and actionable, the record should include a safely redacted target/path category so it can be diagnosed.

### Actual behavior

Every handled ENOENT probe is logged as `[error]`, sometimes hundreds of times per session, obscuring genuine extension failures in the Output channel.

### Impact

Minor; no functional failure observed. The impact is diagnostic noise and reduced usefulness of the extension log.

### Additional information

This is separate from VS Code file-watcher exhaustion/`ENOSPC`; no watcher failure accompanies these batches. Reloading VS Code may clear some stale state temporarily, but the behavior recurs during normal thread activity.

items.title: Voice sessions should be hard-scoped to the selected SSH remote project

labels.name: enhancement

items.body:
## Summary

Codex Desktop supports Realtime Voice for local projects, but Voice should also be available **inside an SSH remote project with that remote project as a hard scope boundary**.

The important requirement is not merely that a local/macOS Voice session can orchestrate work running on a remote host. The Voice session itself should belong to the selected remote project and inherit only that remote project's context, tools, permissions, conversations, and project state.

## Requested behavior

When a remote project is selected, allow starting a Voice conversation that remains pinned to that remote project for its lifetime.

Conceptually:

```text
Remote A → Voice session A → Remote A context/tools/sessions
Remote B → Voice session B → Remote B context/tools/sessions
```

rather than:

```text
Mac/global Voice session → Remote A + Remote B + local projects
```

A Voice session started from Remote A should not silently fall back to a local/projectless session, and it should not require using a broader local Voice coordinator that can see or orchestrate unrelated remotes.

## Why local Voice orchestration is not equivalent

A possible workaround is to start Voice on the Mac and have that session orchestrate Codex tasks running on remote hosts.

That solves a different problem.

Some users intentionally use separate remote environments as organizational and contextual boundaries. Work performed in Remote A should remain scoped to Remote A; work performed in Remote B should remain scoped to Remote B. A higher-level Voice session on the Mac weakens that boundary by making the local coordinator the common context above otherwise independent remotes.

The missing capability is therefore not simply **remote control by voice**. It is **a Voice session whose context and authority are rooted in one selected remote project**.

This is useful even when the local Voice orchestrator is technically capable of creating or steering remote workers.

## Expected scope semantics

A remote-project Voice session should:

- inherit the selected remote project/host;
- use that project's instructions and project context;
- expose only the tools and permissions available through that remote project;
- retain the same project association when switching between text and Voice;
- remain clearly identified as belonging to that remote;
- never silently fall back to a local or projectless context;
- avoid gaining visibility into unrelated local projects or other remotes merely because Voice is running on the desktop client.

This is primarily a context/scope requirement, not a request for microphone access on the remote machine. Audio can remain on the desktop/OpenAI side; the selected remote project should simply remain the Voice session's execution and context boundary.

## Use case

I use Codex Desktop on macOS while keeping different development environments on separate remote hosts. The remotes are useful not only as execution environments but also as clean boundaries between unrelated subjects/projects.

I want to be able to open Remote A and have a Voice conversation whose entire working context is Remote A, then open Remote B and have a separate Voice conversation scoped entirely to Remote B.

Using one Mac-level Voice coordinator for both is intentionally not equivalent for this workflow.

## Related issues / why this is not exactly the same request

- #40391 — **Realtime Voice from SSH remote project falls back to local/projectless session**  
  This is the closest issue. It reports a regression on an Ubuntu desktop client where Voice previously preserved an SSH remote project and now loses that association. This request is broader and product-level: hard remote-project scoping should be a supported behavior across Codex Desktop platforms, including macOS, and should not depend on falling back to a local/global Voice coordinator. If maintainers consider the desired contract identical, this issue can of course be consolidated there.

- #39269 — **Windows: Voice Chat Fork loses parent project context, model selection, and AGENTS startup behavior**  
  This concerns inheritance when Voice forks from a Windows multi-folder project. It is related because project context is lost, but it does not address an SSH remote host as the isolation/scope boundary.

- #33966 — **Codex Live: Duplex voice collaboration with an active Codex session**  
  This asks for continuous shared-state Voice collaboration with a running Codex session. The request here is narrower in one respect and stricter in another: the Voice session must be pinned to one remote project rather than becoming a general orchestration layer.

- #35466 — **Feature request: persistent, project-aware voice navigation**  
  This proposes persistent Voice across projects and explicitly discusses project-specific context. This request focuses on the complementary requirement that a Voice session can be deliberately *hard-pinned* to a single SSH remote project instead of following/globalizing navigation.

- #35687 — **Feature request: add voice conversations to Codex Mobile Remote**  
  This is about a paired mobile client joining a Codex session hosted on a Mac. It does not cover starting a desktop Voice session whose selected project itself lives on an SSH remote host.

- #35248 — **Enable Codex Live for mobile Remote Control sessions hosted by Linux CLI**  
  This concerns mobile Voice attaching to a Linux CLI/app-server Remote Control host. The audio/client topology is different from Codex Desktop directly opening an SSH remote project and keeping Voice scoped to that project.

- #38504 — **Feature request: Live Voice as a first-class Codex orchestration surface**  
  This requests a richer general orchestration surface for Voice. This issue is specifically about the opposite boundary concern: even if Voice becomes a powerful orchestrator, users should be able to root a Voice session in exactly one remote project and keep unrelated environments outside its scope.

## Success criterion

From Codex Desktop, select an SSH remote project, start Realtime Voice, and have the resulting Voice conversation remain visibly and functionally attached to that same remote project for its entire lifetime, with no local/projectless fallback and no need to use a broader desktop-level coordinator.

### Codex CLI version

0.160.0 (npm package)

### Platform

Windows

### Summary

The config reference describes `skills.config.path` as the path to a skill folder containing `SKILL.md`. In Codex CLI 0.160.0, a `path` selector pointing to that folder does not disable the skill. The skill remains in the prompt catalog and can still be selected.

Pointing the selector to the `SKILL.md` file itself works. A `name` selector also works.

### Reproduction

1. Install a skill at `/path/to/skills/example/SKILL.md`.
2. Add this to the user-level `config.toml`:

   ```toml
   [[skills.config]]
   path = "/path/to/skills/example"
   enabled = false
   ```

3. Run `codex debug prompt-input` and inspect the available-skills catalog.

### Observed

The skill is still listed. Changing `path` to `/path/to/skills/example/SKILL.md` removes it from the catalog.

In the 0.160.0 source, the skill metadata stores `path_to_skills_md`, while path rules are compared against that path:
- `codex-rs/skills/src/model.rs`
- `codex-rs/config/src/skills_config.rs`

### Expected

A folder path should be resolved to its `SKILL.md`, as documented, and disable that skill. Alternatively, the config reference should explicitly require the `SKILL.md` file path and provide that form consistently.

Title: Upwork app profile actions advertised by tool help are absent from Codex desktop callable schema

## Environment

- Codex desktop 26.930.3930.0
- Upwork curated app 11.0.0

## Problem

The live Upwork tool help for `update_profile` documents `update_title`, `update_overview`, `set_video`, and `set_skills`. The callable schema exposed by Codex desktop allows only 13 older availability, employment, language, education, and other-experience actions.

The callable `confirm_draft` type enum also omits `profile_update_title`, `profile_update_overview`, `profile_set_video`, and `profile_set_skills`, although live help includes them. The help directs callers to `confirm_preview` and prefers `preview_id`; the exposed callable is `confirm_draft` and requires `draft_id`.

A prior `update_overview` attempt failed with `INVALID_ARGUMENT` because that action was not in the host's allowed enum. The operation was rejected during callable-schema enum validation; no profile-update preview or draft was created. Read-only account/profile calls succeeded.

## Expected

Codex's callable schema should match the live tool contract and allow supported profile actions to produce a review-only preview, with execution still gated by explicit human confirmation.

Please identify the registered callable-schema revision and source, whether filtering or a host snapshot is involved, and the matching live-help schema revision. Also provide the supported refresh or repair path.

Related context: [#41627](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/41627) reports a similar stale-schema symptom for a different curated app (Neon); this report concerns Upwork and does not assume the same root cause.

## Summary

During a live voice session on the Windows desktop app, the user reported that the Codex sidebar stopped showing their pinned chats and named projects. Switching from the Codex surface to ChatGPT and then back to Codex restored the expected pinned chats and projects.

## Environment

- Windows desktop app, Codex surface.
- Observed October 5, 2026.
- Exact desktop app version and Windows build were not collected.
- A voice conversation and project tasks were active. It is not established whether these were causal.

## Observed sequence

1. Use Codex with existing pinned chats and local projects.
2. The user notices that the expected project/chat organization is no longer visible; the displayed interface instead includes items described as priorities and clarification prompts.
3. Switch to ChatGPT.
4. Switch back to Codex.
5. The user confirms that pinned chats and projects are visible again.

The initial trigger is unknown; this is an observed recovery sequence, not a deterministic reproduction recipe.

## Expected behavior

The Codex surface should consistently display its existing pinned chats and projects without requiring a surface switch to restore the sidebar.

The disappearance and recovery were reported directly by the user in the same session. The assistant's screen-context tool exposed the active Codex chat but not the rendered sidebar, so the visual disappearance was not independently captured. Project and thread APIs continued to return existing records. No project deletion, sidebar reorganization, or recovery mutation was performed by the reporting assistant.

Please investigate a possible sidebar/surface state refresh problem. A specific root cause has not been established.

- #42739 concerns projects disappearing after a Windows desktop update, with a different recovery behavior.
- #43025 concerns sidebar organization after restart on macOS.

This report adds the Windows ChatGPT-to-Codex surface-switch recovery symptom; a shared cause is unconfirmed.
